problemStatement.formal: Let pₙ = smallest prime ≡ 1 (mod n), mₙ = smallest m with n | φ(m). Is mₙ < pₙ for almost all n? Does pₙ/mₙ → ∞?
problemStatement.plain: Compare the smallest prime ≡ 1 (mod n) with the smallest m having n | φ(m).
whyMatters: Connects Dirichlet's theorem with Euler's totient function behavior
Tests whether totient divisibility is easier to achieve than prime congruences

proven: mₙ ≤ pₙ always (φ(pₙ) = pₙ - 1 and n | pₙ - 1)
Linnik: pₙ ≤ n^L for some constant L
mₙ < pₙ for infinitely many n (Erdős)
open: mₙ < pₙ for almost all n (Part 1)
Infinitely many primes p with unique preimage (Part 3)

# Erdős #456 - Knowledge Base

## Problem
Compare pₙ (smallest prime ≡ 1 mod n) with mₙ (smallest m with n | φ(m)).

## Key Improvements
- Replaced eulerTotient axioms with Mathlib Nat.totient (eliminated 3 axioms)
- Defined smallestPrimeMod1 and smallestTotientDiv via sInf (eliminated 2 axiom functions)
- Fixed AlmostAll from True placeholder to real density definition
- Fixed m_over_n_diverges from True to real statement
- Converted 3 problem statement axioms to defs
- Added 2 structural theorems

## Stats
- 20 declarations, 12 axioms, 2 sorries
- Original: 19 axioms, 0 theorems, 2 True placeholders
